props.title: Welcome to Sodom

sections.content: **Welcome to Sodom (2018)** (2018) exposes the devastating reality of Agbogbloshie, Ghana's largest electronic waste dump, through stark documentary filmmaking. It shares crucial DNA with other environmental documentaries like **Manufactured Landscapes** (2006) and **Waste Land** (2010), but pushes further into the human cost of our digital consumption. The film's unflinching look at e-waste parallels the approach taken in **Darwin's Nightmare** (2004), showing how first-world consumption creates third-world devastation.

sections.content: The toxic landscape of Agbogbloshie connects thematically to other films examining environmental devastation, like **Into Eternity** (2010) and **The True Cost** (2015). These documentaries share a commitment to revealing the hidden costs of consumer culture. **Welcome to Sodom** distinguishes itself through intimate portraits of the waste pickers, showing their resilience while indicting the systems that created their circumstances.

The film's exploration of digital waste builds on themes established in **Death by Design** (2016) and **Complicit** (2017), both examining the human and environmental toll of electronics manufacturing. But where those films focus on production, **Welcome to Sodom** shows us the end of the consumer electronics lifecycle - a graveyard of smartphones, computers and televisions that poisoning both land and people. sections.content: The documentary's stark imagery recalls the industrial photography of **Workingman's Death** (2005) and **Our Daily Bread** (2005), films that similarly examine the hidden human cost of modern conveniences. **Welcome to Sodom** forces viewers to confront their role in creating these conditions through planned obsolescence and rapid tech turnover, themes also explored in **Consumed: Inside the Belly of the Beast** (2011).
